title: What Does Real Humility in Christian Leadership Look Like?
subtitle: Real humility in Christian leadership is not the performance of smallness but an honest self-forgetfulness that frees a pastor to lead boldly without needing to be praised for it.

sections.title: The Most Proud Men I Know Talk About Humility
sections.body:
There is a kind of humility that is the proudest thing in the room. It announces itself. It says I am just a sinner saved by grace and waits for the disagreement. It deflects the compliment so loudly that everyone notices the deflection. It is pride that has learned the vocabulary of lowliness and uses it to get the same applause by a quieter road.

I have done this. I have fished for reassurance with a self deprecating line. I have made a show of my unworthiness because being known as humble is its own kind of status. The flesh is endlessly creative. It will even counterfeit the virtue that is supposed to kill it.

Real humility does not talk about itself at all. It is too busy thinking about something better than itself.

sections.title: Not Thinking Less of Yourself. Thinking of Yourself Less.
sections.body:
Humility is not the belief that you are worthless. That is not lowliness. That is a different sin, and a miserable one, and it keeps the self at the center just as surely as pride does, only with the lights turned down.

True humility is self forgetfulness. It is the blessed relief of a man who has stopped keeping score on his own performance because his worth was settled at the cross and is no longer up for a vote. He can hear a compliment without inflating and a criticism without collapsing, because neither one is telling him anything about his standing before God that he did not already know.

Not a low view of self. A free man who has stopped staring at himself altogether.

sections.title: The Humble Leader Is the Bold One
sections.body:
We assume the humble pastor is the timid one, the one who never decides, who apologizes his way through every meeting. We have it backward. The man who needs everyone's approval cannot lead. He bends to the loudest voice. He cannot say the hard thing because he cannot bear to be disliked.

The truly humble man is free to be bold, because he is not protecting his image. He does not need the win. He can take the blame that belongs to someone else and give away the credit that belongs to him, because his name is not what he is living for. Moses was the meekest man on the earth, and Moses stood in front of Pharaoh and would not move.

Humility is not the absence of strength. It is strength that has stopped serving itself.

sections.title: Humility Is Forged in Being Overlooked
sections.body:
You do not become humble by reading about it. You become humble by being humbled, and God is faithful to arrange it. The position you wanted and did not get. The younger man who passed you. The criticism that was partly true and stung because it was. The years of faithful work that no one noticed.

These are not detours from formation. They are the formation. God takes a man who wants to be great and walks him through enough small deaths that he stops needing to be. The wilderness years are not wasted years. They are where the savior complex goes to die so that a servant can be born.

Do not despise the hidden seasons. They are where the proud man you would have become is quietly buried.

sections.title: He Washed Their Feet and Knew Who He Was
sections.body:
On the last night, knowing all things had been placed in His hands, Jesus rose, wrapped a towel around His waist, and washed the feet of the men who would abandon Him. John makes the point on purpose. He did it not in spite of His power but in full knowledge of it.

That is the pattern for every Christian leader. Humility is not the denial of your authority. It is the willingness to lay it down at the feet of people who do not deserve it, because the one you follow did exactly that for you.

He knew who He was. That is why He could kneel. Settle the question of who you are in Christ, and you will be free to take the lowest seat without losing yourself in it.
